A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSA research. Their main text, equations, proofs, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, with relocations and renumbering traceable across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, attention analyses, and timing measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the 1B-model evaluations and 300M-model ablations.

M1.justification: The dual-stream sampling procedure, counterpart attention computation, bidirectional alignment losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical; Section 5 expands the motivation without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SmolLM and DCLM training data and evaluate commonsense reasoning, WikiText, PG-19, LongBench, and RULER NIAH. The represented tasks, context-length scenarios, and sparsity coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: FullAttn, MoBA, NSA, and their evaluated variants retain the same comparison membership. The additional methods discussed in v3's related work are not evaluated. NSA was already absent from Figure 4; v3 adds an explanation of that exclusion.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training-token budgets, context lengths, receptive fields, metrics, sample counts, and evaluation procedures are retained. The newly specified continual-training learning rate documents an existing experiment without establishing a changed protocol; RoPE scaling details were already available in v2.

E4.justification: The alignment-weight and L2-loss ablations appearing in v3's Table 3 already existed in v2's Appendix K and Table A14. Sparsity, stream-ratio, NSA-component, KL-divergence, and RoPE analyses are retained without new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five seeded commonsense evaluations with the same uncertainty reporting, single-run LongBench and NIAH evaluations, and inference timings averaged over 30 runs. Appendix E's seed information is unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched result tables and figure graphics retain their numerical results and plotted findings. This includes v2's Table 3 becoming v3's Table 2 and v2's Table A14 being incorporated into v3's Table 3.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.2 replaces the broadly stated loss-penalty equality with an explicit cross-entropy/entropy/KL identity, and Appendix A specifies expectations under the model's full-attention distribution. Proposition 4.1 scopes dropped-key gradient deficiency to the current step. The attention-sparsity definition, principal error bound, and its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: SSA addresses capability and attention gaps through bidirectional alignment, promotes attention sparsity, and supports strong performance across inference modes and context lengths.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies sparse-only underperformance as a possibility and expands the alignment rationale, including a non-degenerate full-attention proviso. Section 7.2 newly cautions that most commonsense contexts are shorter than 1024 tokens, making RF=1024 nearly full attention. Most other interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly specifies a learning rate of 1e-5 for the existing 32k continual-training stage and explicitly confirms that its global batch size remains unchanged. Architecture configurations, implementation libraries, and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through differentiable routing, full-attention distillation, and hybrid architectures, including DashAttention, SeerAttention studies, and HySparse. It now explicitly acknowledges other approaches involving full attention and distinguishes SSA through bidirectional adaptation that also makes full attention sparser. Nine cited works are added.

P1.justification: Selected related-work, theory, method-explanation, and evaluation paragraphs are rewritten or expanded. Further-ablation discussion moves from Appendix K into Section 7.5, and acceptance information, an impact statement, and acknowledgments are added. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 merges the former main and supplementary ablation tables, renumbers the long-context table, and relocates figures and appendix tables. Captions receive limited edits, while the existing figure graphics and general visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by explicitly defining the expectation underlying Proposition 4.2 and narrowing the gradient-deficiency explanation. The RF=1024 qualification, continual-training learning rate, and expanded comparison with related approaches improve interpretation, reproducibility, and positioning. These are useful refinements to a paper whose method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
